text: Now the old banker remembered all this. <break time="0.8s" /> And thought. <break time="0.8s" /> Tomorrow at twelve oclock. <break time="0.8s" /> He will be free. <break time="0.8s" /> If I pay him two million. <break time="0.8s" /> I will be completely ruined. <break time="0.8s" /> Fifteen years before he had more money. <break time="0.8s" /> Than he could count. <break time="0.8s" /> But now he was afraid. <break time="0.8s" /> To ask himself. <break time="0.8s" /> Which he had more of, money or debts. <break time="0.8s" /> Reckless gambling. <break time="0.8s" /> On the stock market. <break time="0.8s" /> Had slowly destroyed his fortune. <break time="0.8s" /> The only way. <break time="0.8s" /> To save myself from shame. <break time="0.8s" /> Is for that man to die. <break time="0.8s" /> He whispered. <break time="0.8s" /> At three oclock in the morning. <break time="0.8s" /> He took the key to the lodge. <break time="0.8s" /> And went quietly. <break time="0.8s" /> Into the garden. <break time="0.8s" /> It was dark and cold. <break time="0.8s" /> And the watchman was asleep somewhere. <break time="0.8s" /> Because of the bad weather. <break time="0.8s" /> Through the window. <break time="0.8s" /> He saw the prisoner. <break time="0.8s" /> Sitting at the table. <break time="0.8s" /> Not moving at all. <break time="0.8s" /> He was only skin and bones. <break time="0.8s" /> With long hair like a womans. <break time="0.8s" /> And a wild, shaggy beard. <break time="0.8s" /> His head was resting on his hands. <break time="0.8s" /> And in front of him lay. <break time="0.8s" /> A sheet of paper. <break time="0.8s" /> Covered with small writing.
